subtitle: Motor Function

educationalGoal:
This course provides an overview of the neuroscience of:
(1) motor control
(2) learning through motor control of the peripheral and central nervous systems
(3) mind, brain, and health, and the intersection of psychology and cognitive neuroscience.
advice: This course provides an overview of the neuroscience of motor control and learning through motor control of the peripheral and central nervous systems, mind, brain, and health, and the intersection of psychology and cognitive neuroscience. Fundamental biological, psychological, social, and environmental factors are introduced with an emphasis on critical functions related to motor control and animal neuroscience of learning, such as sensitive periods, and neuroplasticity. In addition, factors that facilitate and roadblocks that inhibit optimization of learning are explored as we discuss key cognitive constructs (language, attention, memory, executive functions, brain disorders), with special attention on neurocognitive processes and motor control. These studies will be directly applied by each student in future Project Design III activities conducted in an area of each student’s personal interest.
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry is required. High school-level knowledge of biology, and students should have knowledge of basic cell biology, anatomy of human body, and sensory physiology.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course provides an overview of the neuroscience of motor control and learning through motor control of the peripheral and central nervous systems, mind, brain, and health, and the intersection of psychology and cognitive neuroscience. Fundamental biological, psychological, social, and environmental factors are introduced with an emphasis on critical functions related to motor control and animal neuroscience of learning, such as sensitive periods, and neuroplasticity. In addition, factors that facilitate and roadblocks that inhibit optimization of learning are explored as we discuss key cognitive constructs (language, attention, memory, executive functions, brain disorders), with special attention on neurocognitive processes and motor control. These studies will be directly applied by each student in future Project Design III activities conducted in an area of each student’s personal interest.

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              　　

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              Basic knowledge of biochemistry, physics and chemistry is required. High school-level knowledge of biology, and students should have knowledge of basic cell biology, anatomy of human body, and sensory physiology.
